q: The formation of $\ce{PH_4^+}$ is difficult compared to $\ce{NH_4^+}$ because :
question: The formation of $\ce{PH_4^+}$ is difficult compared to $\ce{NH_4^+}$ because :
options: lone pair of phosphorus is optically inert
lone pair of phosphorus resides in almost pure p-orbital
lone pair of phosphorus resides at $sp^3$ orbital
lone pair of phosphorus resides in almost pure s-orbital
solution:
In $NH_3$, the nitrogen atom undergoes $sp^3$ hybridization. The bond angle is 107.8°, and the lone pair of electrons resides in a highly directional $sp^3$ hybrid orbital. This makes the lone pair readily available to be donated to a proton ($H^+$), making the formation of $NH_4^+$ relatively easy.

In contrast, the bond angle in $PH_3$ is approximately 93.6°. Because this angle is very close to 90°, it indicates that the phosphorus atom does not undergo significant hybridization. Instead, it uses its almost pure $p$-orbitals to form bonds with hydrogen. Consequently, the lone pair of electrons on the phosphorus atom is left residing in an almost pure, unhybridized $s$-orbital ($3s$).

Since $s$-orbitals are spherically symmetrical, non-directional, and located closer to the nucleus, the lone pair is held tightly by the phosphorus nucleus and is not easily donated to a proton. Thus, the formation of $PH_4^+$ is difficult.

Correct Option: Option D

question:
Which is the correct sequence in the following properties? For the correct order mark (T) and for the incorrect order mark (F):

(a) Lewis acidity order: SiF4 < SiCl4 < SiBr4 < SiI4

(b) Melting point: NH3 > SbH3 > AsH3 > PH3

(c) Boiling point: NH3 > SbH3 > AsH3 > PH3

(d) Bond dipole order: NH3 > SbH3 > AsH3 > PH3
options: FTFT
TFTF
FFTT
FFTF
solution:
(a) Lewis acidity order: $\text{SiF}_4 < \text{SiCl}_4 < \text{SiBr}_4 < \text{SiI}_4$

In silicon tetrahalides, the central silicon atom has empty $d$-orbitals available to accept electron pairs. Fluorine is the most electronegative halogen, creating the highest positive charge density on the silicon atom in $\text{SiF}_4$. Additionally, as the size of the halogen increases from fluorine to iodine, steric crowding around the silicon atom increases, making it harder for incoming donor species to approach. Therefore, the Lewis acidity actually decreases down the group:

$$\text{SiF}_4 > \text{SiCl}_4 > \text{SiBr}_4 > \text{SiI}_4$$

Thus, statement (a) is False (F).

(b) Melting point: $\text{NH}_3 > \text{SbH}_3 > \text{AsH}_3 > \text{PH}_3$

Ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds in the solid state, which gives it the highest melting point among these hydrides. For the remaining hydrides, the melting point increases down the group from $\text{PH}_3$ to $\text{SbH}_3$ as molecular size and van der Waals forces increase.

The observed melting points are:

  • $\text{NH}_3$: $195.2\text{ K}$

  • $\text{SbH}_3$: $185.0\text{ K}$

  • $\text{AsH}_3$: $156.7\text{ K}$

  • $\text{PH}_3$: $139.5\text{ K}$

Hence, the melting point order is indeed $\text{NH}_3 > \text{SbH}_3 > \text{AsH}_3 > \text{PH}_3$.

Thus, statement (b) is True (T).

(c) Boiling point: $\text{NH}_3 > \text{SbH}_3 > \text{AsH}_3 > \text{PH}_3$

In the liquid state, the increase in molecular mass and van der Waals forces from $\text{PH}_3$ to $\text{SbH}_3$ becomes dominant enough that $\text{SbH}_3$ ($254\text{ K}$) has a higher boiling point than $\text{NH}_3$ ($238.5\text{ K}$).

The correct boiling point order is:

$$\text{SbH}_3 > \text{NH}_3 > \text{AsH}_3 > \text{PH}_3$$

Thus, statement (c) is False (F).

(d) Bond dipole order: $\text{NH}_3 > \text{SbH}_3 > \text{AsH}_3 > \text{PH}_3$

The bond dipole moment depends on the difference in Pauling electronegativity ($\Delta\chi$) between the central atom and hydrogen ($\chi_{\text{H}} \approx 2.1$):

  • For $\text{N}-\text{H}$: $|\Delta\chi| = |3.0 - 2.1| = 0.9$

  • For $\text{Sb}-\text{H}$: $|\Delta\chi| = |1.9 - 2.1| = 0.2$

  • For $\text{As}-\text{H}$: $|\Delta\chi| = |2.0 - 2.1| = 0.1$

  • For $\text{P}-\text{H}$: $|\Delta\chi| = |2.1 - 2.1| = 0.0$

Since the magnitude of the electronegativity difference follows the order $\text{N}-\text{H} > \text{Sb}-\text{H} > \text{As}-\text{H} > \text{P}-\text{H}$, the bond dipole order is $\text{NH}_3 > \text{SbH}_3 > \text{AsH}_3 > \text{PH}_3$.

Thus, statement (d) is True (T).

The correct sequence is FTFT.

question:
Given below are two statements.

Statement I : N(CH3)3 and P(CH3)3 can act as ligands to form transition metal complexes.

Statement II : As N and P are from same group, the nature of bonding of N(CH3)3 and P(CH3)3 is always same with transition metals.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
solution:
• Statement I is correct: Both $N(CH_3)_3$ (trimethylamine)$ and P(CH_3)_3$ (trimethylphosphine) possess a lone pair of electrons on the central atom (nitrogen and phosphorus, respectively). They can donate this lone pair to transition metals, allowing them to act as ligands and form coordination complexes.

  • Statement II is incorrect: Although nitrogen and phosphorus belong to the same group (Group 15), the nature of their bonding with transition metals differs significantly. Nitrogen lacks vacant $d$-orbitals in its valence shell, meaning $N(CH_3)_3$ can only act as a $\sigma$-donor ligand. In contrast, phosphorus has vacant $3d$-orbitals. This allows $P(CH_3)_3$ to act as a $\sigma$-donor and also accept electron density back from the metal's filled $d$-orbitals into its empty $d$-orbitals (a process known as $p\pi$-$d\pi$ back-bonding or $\pi$-back donation). Therefore, their bonding nature is not the same.

Correct Option: Option A

  • Statement II is incorrect: Although nitrogen and phosphorus belong to the same group (Group 15), the nature of their bonding with transition metals differs significantly. Nitrogen lacks vacant $d$-orbitals in its valence shell, meaning $N(CH_3)_3$ can only act as a $\sigma$-donor ligand. In contrast, phosphorus has vacant $3d$-orbitals. Therefore, their bonding nature is not the same.

Correct Option: Option A

question:
Given below are two statements.

Statement I : The pentavalent oxide of group-15 element, $E_2 O_5$, is less acidic than trivalent oxide, $\mathrm{E}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ of the same element.

Statement II : The acidic character of trivalent oxide of group-15 elements, $E_2 O_3$, decreases down the group.

In light of the above statements, choose most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
solution:
• Statement I is incorrect: The acidic character of an oxide depends on the oxidation state of the central atom. An oxide in a higher oxidation state is more acidic than one in a lower oxidation state. Therefore, the pentavalent oxide ($E_2O_5$, where the oxidation state is $+5$) is more acidic than the trivalent oxide ($E_2O_3$, where the oxidation state is $+3$) of the same element.

  • Statement II is correct: As we move down Group 15, the atomic size increases and the elements become more metallic in nature. Since non-metal oxides are acidic and metal oxides are basic, the acidic character of the trivalent oxides ($E_2O_3$) decreases down the group. For example, $N_2O_3$ and $P_2O_3$ are purely acidic, $As_2O_3$ and $Sb_2O_3$ are amphoteric, and $Bi_2O_3$ is predominantly basic.

Because Statement I is false and Statement II is true, the correct choice is Option D.

Correct Option: Option D
explanation:
• Statement I is incorrect: The acidic character of an oxide depends on the oxidation state of the central atom. An oxide in a higher oxidation state is more acidic than one in a lower oxidation state. Therefore, the pentavalent oxide ($E_2O_5$, where the oxidation state is $+5$) is more acidic than the trivalent oxide ($E_2O_3$, where the oxidation state is $+3$) of the same element.

  • Statement II is correct: As we move down Group 15, the atomic size increases and the elements become more metallic in nature. Since non-metal oxides are acidic and metal oxides are basic, the acidic character of the trivalent oxides ($E_2O_3$) decreases down the group. For example, $N_2O_3$ and $P_2O_3$ are purely acidic, $As_2O_3$ and $Sb_2O_3$ are amphoteric, and $Bi_2O_3$ is predominantly basic.

Because Statement I is false and Statement II is true, the correct choice is Option D.

Correct Option: Option D

question:
White phosphorus on reaction with limewater gives calcium salt of an acid $(A)$ along with a gas $(X)$. The number of incorrect statement is

(i) $(A)$ on heating gives $(X)$ and $O_2$.

(ii) the bond angle in $(X)$ is less than that in case of ammonia.

(iii) $(A)$ is a dibasic acid.

(iv) $(X)$ is more basic than ammonia.
solution:
White phosphorus reacts with limewater to give calcium hypophosphite and phosphine gas.

The reaction is:

$$ P_4 + Ca(OH)_2 + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(H_2PO_2)_2 + PH_3 $$

So,

$$ (A) = H_3PO_2 $$

This acid is hypophosphorous acid.

$$ (X) = PH_3 $$

This gas is phosphine.

Now check the statements.

(i) $H_3PO_2$ on heating does not give $PH_3$ and $O_2$. It disproportionates mainly as:

$$ 2H_3PO_2 \rightarrow PH_3 + H_3PO_4 $$

So statement (i) is incorrect.

(ii) The bond angle in $PH_3$ is about $93.5^\circ$, while in $NH_3$ it is about $107^\circ$.

So the bond angle in $PH_3$ is less than that in ammonia.

Statement (ii) is correct.

(iii) $H_3PO_2$ has only one ionisable hydrogen because it contains only one $P-OH$ bond. The other two hydrogens are directly attached to phosphorus.

So $H_3PO_2$ is monobasic, not dibasic.

Statement (iii) is incorrect.

(iv) $PH_3$ is less basic than $NH_3$ because the lone pair on phosphorus is less available for donation.

So statement (iv) is incorrect.

Incorrect statements are:

$$ (i), (iii), (iv) $$

Hence, the number of incorrect statements is:

$$ \boxed{3} $$

White phosphorus reacts with limewater to give calcium hypophosphite and phosphine gas.

The reaction is:

$$ P_4 + Ca(OH)_2 + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(H_2PO_2)_2 + PH_3 $$

So,

$$ (A) = H_3PO_2 $$

This acid is hypophosphorous acid.

$$ (X) = PH_3 $$

This gas is phosphine.

Now check the statements.

(i) $H_3PO_2$ on heating does not give $PH_3$ and $O_2$. It disproportionates mainly as:

$$ 2H_3PO_2 \rightarrow PH_3 + H_3PO_4 $$

So statement (i) is incorrect.

(ii) The bond angle in $PH_3$ is about $93.5^\circ$, while in $NH_3$ it is about $107^\circ$.

So the bond angle in $PH_3$ is less than that in ammonia.

Statement (ii) is correct.

(iii) $H_3PO_2$ has only one ionisable hydrogen because it contains only one $P-OH$ bond. The other two hydrogens are directly attached to phosphorus.

So $H_3PO_2$ is monobasic, not dibasic.

Statement (iii) is incorrect.

(iv) $PH_3$ is less basic than $NH_3$ because the lone pair on phosphorus is less available for donation.

So statement (iv) is incorrect.

Incorrect statements are:

$$ (i), (iii), (iv) $$

Hence, the number of incorrect statements is:

$$ \boxed{3} $$

A poisonous, waxy solid \left(P_x O_y\right)$ is soluble in benzene and has a garlic odour. It is formed by the reaction of phosphorus with nitrous oxide. It undergoes disproportionation reaction with hot water. Then then sum of $x$ and $y$ is

$
question:
A poisonous, waxy solid \left(P_x O_y\right)$ is soluble in benzene and has a garlic odour. It is formed by the reaction of phosphorus with nitrous oxide. It undergoes disproportionation reaction with hot water. Then then sum of $x$ and $y$ is

$
solution:
The compound described is phosphorus trioxide, whose molecular formula is $P_4O_6$.

It matches the given properties:

  • It is a poisonous, waxy solid.

  • It has a garlic-like odour.

  • It is soluble in benzene.

  • It is formed when phosphorus reacts with nitrous oxide:

$$ P_4 + 6N_2O \rightarrow P_4O_6 + 6N_2 $$

It also undergoes disproportionation with hot water:

$$ P_4O_6 + 6H_2O \rightarrow PH_3 + 3H_3PO_4 $$

Here, phosphorus in $P_4O_6$ has oxidation state $+3$. It changes to $-3$ in $PH_3$ and $+5$ in $H_3PO_4$, so it is a disproportionation reaction.

Thus,

$$ x = 4,\quad y = 6 $$

So,

$$ x+y = 4+6 = 10 $$

The answer is:

$$ \boxed{10} $$

In hyponitrous acid, if $X$ is number of $\sigma$ bonds, $Y$ is number of non bonding pairs and $Z$ is the number of $\pi$ bond the value of \left(X+Z-\frac{Y}{2}\right)$ is

$
question:
In hyponitrous acid, if $X$ is number of $\sigma$ bonds, $Y$ is number of non bonding pairs and $Z$ is the number of $\pi$ bond the value of \left(X+Z-\frac{Y}{2}\right)$ is

$
solution:
The molecular formula of hyponitrous acid is $\text{H}_2\text{N}_2\text{O}_2$.

Its structural formula is:

Let us find the required values by looking at the structure:

1. Number of $\sigma$ bonds ($X$):

  • Two single $\text{O}-\text{H}$ bonds contribute $2\ \sigma$ bonds.

  • Two single $\text{N}-\text{O}$ bonds contribute $2\ \sigma$ bonds.

  • One double $\text{N}=\text{N}$ bond contains $1\ \sigma$ bond.

$$X = 2 + 2 + 1 = 5$$

2. Number of $\pi$ bonds ($Z$):

  • The double bond between the two nitrogen atoms contains $1\ \pi$ bond.

$$Z = 1$$

3. Number of non-bonding electron pairs ($Y$):

  • Each oxygen atom has 2 lone pairs, so two oxygen atoms have $2 \times 2 = 4$ lone pairs.

  • Each nitrogen atom has 1 lone pair, so two nitrogen atoms have $2 \times 1 = 2$ lone pairs.

$$Y = 4 + 2 = 6$$

Now, substituting these values into the given expression:

$$X + Z - \frac{Y}{2} = 5 + 1 - \frac{6}{2}$$

$$= 6 - 3 = 3$$

The value of $\left(X+Z-\frac{Y}{2}\right)$ is $3$.

$$ $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CaC}_2+\mathrm{N}_2 & \longrightarrow A \\ A+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} & \longrightarrow \text { Gas } B \end{aligned}$ $$

Gas $B$ is also formed by heating $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4\right)_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$, then the oxidation state of central atom in Gas ' B ' is $\_\_\_\_$.

(Exclude negative charge is present)
question:
$$ $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CaC}_2+\mathrm{N}_2 & \longrightarrow A \\ A+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} & \longrightarrow \text { Gas } B \end{aligned}$ $$

Gas $B$ is also formed by heating $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4\right)_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$, then the oxidation state of central atom in Gas ' B ' is $\_\_\_\_$.

(Exclude negative charge is present)
solution:
When calcium carbide ($\mathrm{CaC}_2$) reacts with nitrogen gas ($\mathrm{N}_2$) at high temperature, it forms calcium cyanamide ($\mathrm{CaCN}_2$) along with carbon:

$$\mathrm{CaC}_2 + \mathrm{N}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaCN}_2 + \mathrm{C}$$

Here, compound $A$ is calcium cyanamide ($\mathrm{CaCN}_2$).

When calcium cyanamide is treated with water (steam), it hydrolyses to produce ammonia gas ($\mathrm{NH}_3$):

$$\mathrm{CaCN}_2 + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaCO}_3 + 2\mathrm{NH}_3$$

Thus, Gas $B$ is ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$).

Heating ammonium sulphate also liberates ammonia gas:

$$(\mathrm{NH}_4)_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{HSO}_4 + \mathrm{NH}_3$$

In the ammonia molecule ($\mathrm{NH}_3$), the central atom is nitrogen ($\mathrm{N}$).

To find the oxidation state of nitrogen ($x$):

$$x + 3(+1) = 0$$

$$x = -3$$

Excluding the negative sign as instructed, the required value is $3$.
